problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ x \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =-6\cdot (-2)+(-3)\cdot x+0\cdot (-3) \\  & =12-3x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 12-3x & =0 \\ -3x & =-12 \\ x & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
